description: An enhanced Sunshine fork for Moonlight with HDR10/HDR Vivid, virtual displays, and optimized encoders.
notes: Install from an elevated shell (scoop install -g foundation-sunshine): the bundled virtual display driver (ZakoVDD),
the ViGEmBus virtual gamepad, the SunshineService (auto-start) and the firewall rules are then set up automatically,
and the install directory is locked down to Administrators/SYSTEM (Users get read+execute), which service mode requires.
Update an elevated install with an elevated shell: scoop update -g foundation-sunshine.
Uninstall with an elevated shell: scoop uninstall -g foundation-sunshine. It stops and deletes the SunshineService,
uninstalls ZakoVDD, ViGEmBus and the Zako virtual mouse, removes the firewall rules, the Explorer context menus and the startup shortcut;
add -p to also delete the persisted config (pairing keys, apps list). A restart may be needed after the
Without elevation only the files are installed; run these once from an admin shell afterwards:
Sunshine can be configured at https://localhost:47990/ by default.
pre_install: # sunshine.exe expects to be started from its own directory.
# Service mode runs as SYSTEM, so a user-writable install directory is a privilege-escalation hole and gets rejected.
# Lock it down to Administrators/SYSTEM for writing, Users keep read+execute (the same ACL Program Files has).
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Write-Host 'Install directory ACL tightened (Administrators/SYSTEM write, Users read+execute).' -ForegroundColor Cyan }
else { Write-Host 'Warning: could not tighten the install directory ACL.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }
post_install: # Drivers and services are system-wide, so only do this when we are already elevated.
# The scoop shim prefers PowerShell 7 when it is installed, and PS7 puts its own module directories
# first in PSModulePath. The bundled installers shell out to "powershell" (5.1), which then loads
# the incompatible PS7 Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility and silently loses Get-FileHash, Select-String...
# which makes the ViGEmBus installer fail its own hash check. Restore the native 5.1 search path.
Write-Host 'Elevated install detected, setting up bundled drivers, service and firewall rules...' -ForegroundColor Cyan

if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'System32\drivers\ViGEmBus.sys'))) { Write-Host 'Warning: the ViGEmBus driver is not installed; the virtual gamepad will be unavailable.' -ForegroundColor Yellow }
# A scoop install is non-interactive, so pick the useful default instead of the installer's 'demand'.
& sc.exe config SunshineService start= auto | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { Write-Host 'SunshineService registered with automatic start.' -ForegroundColor Cyan }
Write-Host 'Skipped driver/service setup: re-run from an elevated shell (or use ''scoop install -g'') to have it done automatically.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
pre_uninstall: # scoop deletes the install directory right after this hook, so everything the installer brought into the
# system has to go first: a running sunshinesvc.exe would also lock the binaries and make the removal fail.
# Same PS7/PS5.1 module-path problem as in post_install: the uninstallers shell out to powershell.
# 1. release the binaries: service host, stream host and any tray instance.
# 2. the portable uninstaller's steps, minus its prompts, in dependency order.
# The virtual mouse is a separate driver package with its own uninstaller.
# The ViGEmBus MSI deletes the driver file but can leave the kernel service registered.
# 3. firewall rules an older install (other app directory) or the old installer (Sunshine-All*) left behind.
# 4. per-user leftovers of the portable installer.
# NVENC preference bookkeeping the stream host writes into ProgramData, outside the install directory.
# 4b. 'scoop uninstall -p' deletes the persisted config afterwards. The stream host locks
# config\local-auth.token down to SYSTEM (Administrators only get read), so scoop's own Remove-Item
# dies with the misleading 'may be in use'. Take ownership, drop the explicit ACLs and purge it here.
# 5. give SCM and any pending driver removal a moment to release their handles.
Write-Host ('Service, drivers and firewall rules removed (' + $summary + ', killed ' + $killed + ' process(es)).') -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host 'A restart is required to finish removing the virtual display driver.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
Write-Host 'Not elevated: the SunshineService and the virtual drivers will be left installed.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
